l4_steps.name: Capture work order completion data in MRO system
l4_steps.input: Completed maintenance task card or work order
l4_steps.output: Closed work order record with technician stamp, part numbers, and man-hours
l4_steps.kpi: Work order closure within 2 hours of task completion; >98% same-shift closure rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper-based job cards still used at some line stations — manual re-keying into AMOS introduces transcription errors and delays record closure past the shift boundary

l4_steps.name: Ingest aircraft technical logbook entries
l4_steps.input: Aircraft Technical Log (ATL) — paper or Electronic Technical Log (ETL) feed
l4_steps.output: Digitised logbook entry linked to flight sector and aircraft tail number
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ATL entries ingested before next departure; ETL integration uptime ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: ETL interfaces to PSS (Amadeus Altéa) are non-standardised across fleet sub-types; legacy B737-700 may lack ETL hardware, requiring manual paper log reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Validate record completeness against work order schema
l4_steps.input: Ingested work order and logbook entry
l4_steps.output: Completeness check result — pass or list of missing mandatory fields
l4_steps.kpi: Record completeness rate ≥99.5%; incomplete records resolved within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS mandatory-field validation rules vary by maintenance type (line vs. heavy); misconfigured validation profiles cause false-pass records that fail FAA audit spot-checks

l4_steps.name: Cross-reference task against approved AMM/SRM data
l4_steps.input: Closed work order with task card reference
l4_steps.output: Confirmation that executed task matches approved maintenance data revision
l4_steps.kpi: Zero maintenance releases citing a superseded AMM revision; 100% AMM revision currency per Boeing Service Letter cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing Toolbox AMM revision pushes can lag up to 72 hours behind FAA-approval date; tasks executed on interim revisions may require retroactive re-documentation, increasing rework cost

l4_steps.name: Verify certifying technician licence and authorisation
l4_steps.input: Technician employee ID extracted from work order sign-off
l4_steps.output: Authorisation check result — licence type, rating, and currency status
l4_steps.kpi: Zero maintenance releases by technicians with expired or out-of-scope ratings; authorisation check automated for 100% of closures
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS authorisation matrix must be kept synchronised with FAA A&P licence renewals and airline-specific OJT records; manual update lag creates windows where expired ratings are not flagged

l4_steps.name: Confirm maintenance release and CRS sign-off
l4_steps.input: Verified work order, authorisation check pass, logbook entry
l4_steps.output: Certificate of Release to Service (CRS) or Maintenance Release Statement recorded in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: CRS issued within 30 minutes of final inspection; 100% of CRS statements traceable to FAR Part 43 / EASA Part-145 signatory
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-registry aircraft (operating under both FAA and EASA authority) require CRS language compliant with both regulations; AMOS templates are not always jurisdiction-aware, requiring manual text override

l4_steps.name: Update component life-tracking and next-due dates
l4_steps.input: Closed and certified work order with part removals, installations, and time since new (TSN) data
l4_steps.output: Updated component life record showing revised TSN, cycles since new (CSN), and next maintenance due date
l4_steps.kpi: Component record updated within 8 hours of part installation; life-limit threshold accuracy ±0 flight hours/cycles
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP synchronisation with AMOS relies on nightly batch feeds; intraday part swaps on critical life-limited parts (LLPs) may not appear in CAMP until next morning, creating a brief compliance exposure window

l4_steps.name: Link AD/SB compliance closure record to aircraft serial
l4_steps.input: AD or Service Bulletin number, effectivity, compliance method, and accomplishment date
l4_steps.output: AD compliance entry linked to tail number and fleet record in CAMP
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of applicable ADs reflected in CAMP within 24 hours of task closure; zero open ADs past compliance deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA AD effectivity determination for mixed-variant fleets (737-700/800/MAX 8) is complex; incorrect variant mapping in CAMP can result in ADs being erroneously marked not-applicable, triggering FAA enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Identify overdue or near-threshold compliance items
l4_steps.input: CAMP automated compliance forecast report run daily
l4_steps.output: Prioritised exception list of ADs, LLP limits, and scheduled tasks within 30-day or 100-FH threshold
l4_steps.kpi: Zero items entering the overdue state; 100% of near-threshold items actioned ≥7 days before due date
l4_steps.pain_point: High-frequency short-haul operations (4–6 sector days) can erode compliance buffers faster than weekly planning cycles anticipate; CAMP threshold alerts must be tuned to fleet utilisation intensity to avoid false urgency fatigue

l4_steps.name: Escalate critical airworthiness findings to MCC and Planning
l4_steps.input: Exception list from CAMP with overdue or critical near-threshold items
l4_steps.output: Work order raised in AMOS; maintenance slot requested from MCC; aircraft grounding risk flagged if threshold cannot be met in-service
l4_steps.kpi: MCC notified within 2 hours of threshold breach identification; grounding avoided in ≥95% of escalations through proactive slot allocation
l4_steps.pain_point: MCC operational priority (avoiding flight cancellations) conflicts with airworthiness deadline compliance; without a formal escalation SLA in AMOS, airworthiness items can be deferred repeatedly until a hard grounding is unavoidable

l4_steps.name: Archive work orders per FAA retention schedule
l4_steps.input: Certified and closed work orders exported from AMOS
l4_steps.output: Immutable PDF/A records stored in versioned S3 bucket with metadata tags (tail, date, task reference)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of closed work orders archived within 24 hours; retention period ≥24 months per FAR Part 121.380 for routine tasks, ≥life of aircraft for major repairs
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.380 retention tiers (24-month vs. life-of-aircraft) require automated classification at point of archival; miscategorisation of major repairs as routine tasks has resulted in premature record purges discovered only during aircraft sale due diligence

l4_steps.name: Generate aircraft technical status summary report
l4_steps.input: CAMP compliance data, AMOS work order history, AWS S3 archive index
l4_steps.output: Aircraft Technical Status Report (ATSR) per tail: open deferrals, AD status, LLP remaining life, next check due
l4_steps.kpi: ATSR published weekly for all active tails; zero data discrepancies between ATSR and AMOS/CAMP source systems
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pull from AMOS and CAMP via separate API connectors with different refresh cadences; stale data in one source can make the ATSR appear current while masking an overdue item

l4_steps.name: Validate archived record format for regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Archived PDF/A records sampled from S3 for format and metadata audit
l4_steps.output: Validation report confirming PDF/A-1b compliance, metadata completeness, and tamper-evident hash integrity
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of sampled records pass PDF/A validation; zero records with missing mandatory metadata fields; hash verification failure rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: PDF/A conversion from AMOS native format occasionally strips embedded digital signatures required by FAA AC 120-78B for electronic records; silent conversion failures are only detected during authority audit

l4_steps.name: Compile records package for FAA/authority audit
l4_steps.input: FAA audit notice specifying scope (tail numbers, date range, AD references)
l4_steps.output: Structured audit evidence package: certified work orders, CRS statements, AD compliance records, technician authorisation records
l4_steps.kpi: Audit package delivered within 5 business days of FAA request; zero findings of missing required records in formal audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-system evidence assembly (AMOS + CAMP + AWS S3 + Boeing Toolbox) is manual; no single orchestration tool exists to compile a complete audit package automatically, creating significant labour cost and risk of omissions under tight FAA timelines

l4_steps.name: Respond to AD compliance queries from airworthiness authority
l4_steps.input: FAA/authority query specifying AD number, effectivity date, and fleet scope
l4_steps.output: Formal compliance response citing accomplishment dates, methods of compliance, and tail-by-tail status exported from CAMP
l4_steps.kpi: AD compliance query response within 10 business days; 100% of responses supported by primary source documentation traceable to original work order
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP AD compliance reports are formatted for internal use; exporting in FAA-specified formats (e.g., 8130-3 data elements) requires manual reformatting that introduces transcription risk and delays formal response

l4_steps.name: Submit airworthiness certificate renewal documentation
l4_steps.system: FAA DragonWave / FAA PTRS (Programme Tracking & Reporting Subsystem)
l4_steps.input: Compiled ATSR, AD compliance summary, major repair/alteration records, current maintenance programme approval
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness Certificate renewal package submitted to FAA FSDO; certificate issued or discrepancy list returned
l4_steps.kpi: Certificate renewal submitted ≥30 days before expiry; zero aircraft operated with lapsed airworthiness certificate; discrepancy resolution within 15 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA FSDO processing times are variable and outside airline control; late submission driven by internal records gaps can result in aircraft AOG during the renewal window, incurring significant revenue loss and customer disruption
